L38@P1-2: 2I. DISCOVERY OF THE OKLO NATURAL REACTORS
L39@P2: On 25 September 1972, Andr`e Giraud, Head of the French Commissariat `a l’Energy ´
L40@P2: Atomique (CEA), announced the discovery of a two billion year-old nuclear reactor in Gabon,
L41@P2: at the site of the Oklo uranium mines. The sequence of events that led to this startling
L42@P2: announcement had begun earlier, in June 1972, at the Pierrelatte uranium enrichment plant
L43@P2: with the observation of a small but definite anomaly in the uranium isotopic ratio for a UF6
L44@P2: sample. The supply of anomalous uranium was soon traced to uranium rich ores (up to
L45@P2: 60%) for which investigations revealed local uraninite deposits with 235U isotopic abundance
L46@P2: of 0.600%, instead of the normal 0.7202%.
L47@P2: At first glance one can wonder how the Oklo reactors were able to operate when it is well
L48@P2: known that the modern light water reactors cannot work with natural uranium, requiring
L49@P2: instead 235U enrichment of about 3.5%. Natural uranium is composed of three isotopes with
L50@P2: abundances today1 of 99.2744% for 238U, 0.7202% for 235U, and 0.0054% for 234U. However,
L51@P2: the relative enrichment of 235U increases going back in geological time because the half-life
L52@P2: of 235U is 710 Myr while that of 238U is 4.51 Gyr. For example, 235U enrichment was 1.3%
L53@P2: 700 Myr ago, 2.3% 1.40 Gyr ago, 4.0% 2.10 Gyr ago, and up to 17% at the time of creation
L54@P2: of the solar system.

L174@P6: Oklo based on the negative void temperature coefficient. According to this mechanism, with
L175@P6: increasing reactor temperature, neutron moderating water is converted into steam which can
L176@P6: even leave the active core. As a result, the reactor shuts down, cools off, and only restarts
L177@P6: when water seeps back into the reactor zone again.

L196@P7: III. MONTE-CARLO SIMULATIONS OF OKLO REACTORS
L197@P7: To date, the Oklo uranium deposits are the only known place on Earth where two billion

L199@P7: (i) a high concentration of uranium in different zones, with the 235U abundance being at

L225@P8: The MCNP code input for any Oklo reactor consists of a description of its geometry with
L226@P8: relevant physical dimensions, the operating temperature, and specification of the amounts
L227@P8: of uraninite (a variety of UO2), gangue and water. Typically, reactor zones are lens shaped
L228@P8: layers, about 10 m long, about 10 m wide and up to 0.8 m thick. The uraninite content
L229@P8: varies from zone to zone reaching as high as 80wt.% in some samples. The gangue is
L230@P8: composed of clays – the hydrated silica-aluminates of different metals. Data for several
L231@P8: zones are detailed in Ref. [13]. The amount of water during the time of reactor operation
L232@P8: remains very uncertain. Water, however, defines the shape of the neutron spectrum and
L233@P8: can therefore be deduced by varying its amount until the spectral indices3
L234@P8: of the calculated
L235@P8: neutron flux coincide with the indices deduced from the isotopic data. The output of MCNP
L236@P8: consists of the criticality value and the energy dependence of the neutron spectrum.
